summary: The tape is a stream of 37-byte packets with a 32-bit millisecond clock and eight 24-bit samples. 11122 packets survived the damage; the parser resynchronised after 1499 skipped bytes. The clock steps 4 ms, so the board ran at about 250 samples per second. Channels [1, 2, 3, 4] carry a real signal. Labels come only from the surviving cue rows; nothing was invented for the missing ones.
